{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABYt1Iig", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhCS2Y8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 19, "title": "Implement WonderSwan Color Sound DMA and Hyper Voice with accurate audio mixing", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently supports the four legacy WonderSwan audio channels, basic speaker/headphone output and a Web Audio frontend, but it does **not** emulate **Sound DMA (SDMA)** or **Hyper Voice**. In `crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs`, accesses to SDMA registers `0x4A–0x52` and the Hyper Voice register block are unsupported. `crates/ws-core/src/audio.rs` generates only the four legacy channels, with approximate mixing and output levels.

Software that uses automatic PCM playback or the color models' additional PCM channel cannot produce correct audio, and may stop on unsupported I/O. Adding permissive dummy ports would conceal missing behavior rather than emulate it.

Implement the documented hardware **generically in the from-scratch Rust core**, not using game-specific workarounds, signatures, ROM hashes, or borrowed emulator code. No commercial ROM, proprietary boot ROM, or unlicensed assets may be added to the repository or required for mandatory tests.

## Expected outcome

On **WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal**, original machine-code programs can configure and run Sound DMA into either Channel 2 PCM or Hyper Voice, hear the generated signal through the existing Web Audio output, and observe hardware-consistent register state, transfer progression and sound mixing.

The original monochrome WonderSwan retains its documented capabilities without falsely gaining color-only SDMA/Hyper Voice hardware. Existing four-channel audio, 224×144 gameplay, model selection, cartridge saves, General DMA, default-on sound preference, Mute/Unmute, volume slider, and GitHub Pages deployment must remain functional.

This is a **sound-hardware compatibility** milestone, not a claim of complete commercial-game compatibility or perfect analogue output.

## Context and reproduction

At the time of drafting:

- `crates/ws-core/src/audio.rs` implements four channels, a 24 kHz sample clock and a bounded stereo output queue. Speaker-level handling and mixing/filtering are approximate; there is no Hyper Voice data path.
- `crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs` advances the existing audio system from the common 3.072 MHz machine clock. The `input`/`output` port handlers do not implement SDMA (`0x4A–0x52`) or Hyper Voice (`0x64–0x6B`).
- `crates/ws-core/src/lib.rs` schedules CPU frames and General DMA; changes must integrate into this timebase, not introduce an unrelated timer.
- `crates/ws-web` exposes audio samples to `web/src/audio.ts`, which already handles a single Web Audio context, output GainNode, mute, volume and browser lifecycle. Do not duplicate sound synthesis in JavaScript.
- `fixtures/` already has deterministic original CC0 hardware probes and a Python/NASM build pipeline. Extend it with targeted original fixtures rather than adding dependencies or third-party ROMs.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Use English and separate pre-merge tests from post-merge deployment verification.

Relevant independent **hardware specifications** (use for behavior, not for copying other emulator code):

- [WSdev: DMA / Sound DMA](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/DMA)
- [WSdev: Hyper Voice](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Hyper_Voice)
- [WSdev: Sound and mixing](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Sound)
- [WSdev: Timing](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Timing)
- [WSdev: Memory map](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Memory_map)

### A. Sound DMA controller

1. Implement the documented **SDMA source address (`0x4A–0x4C`), length (`0x4E–0x50`) and control (`0x52`)** registers, with 20-bit effective addresses/lengths, reserved-bit masking, correct readback, and the live-versus-shadowed source/length copies. Determine and document the behavior of the intervening unused ports `0x4D` and `0x51` from the specification; do not silently expose arbitrary undocumented state.
2. Implement SDMA enable/disable; bytewise increment/decrement source traversal; length decrement; stopping and enable-bit clearing on one-shot completion; and **repeat** restoring the shadow source/length. Edits while active must update the visible registers and the documented shadow copy correctly. Disabling/re-enabling should continue at the existing counters rather than implicitly restarting.
3. Implement all documented rates **4, 6, 12, and 24 kHz** and the **hold** bit (advance its timer while substituting zero and not consuming source/length). A zero-length request must not start an active transfer. Test behavior when length reaches zero, including auto-repeat, direction and stop/restart.
4. Route SDMA values to the selected **Channel 2 voice register / PCM path (`0x89`)** or **Hyper Voice input path**, with the required enabling/configuration registers. DMA must read through the existing internal RAM/cartridge/mapper/SRAM bus, including supported slower sources; unlike General DMA, it must not reject byte-wide SRAM or slower ROM solely for their access width/wait states.
5. Model the controller's shared-clock **bus-steal/CPU-stall timing**, including the documented 128-cycle cadence, event phase and `6 + N` access cost per transfer (N = source access time), and coordinate it with CPU instructions, General DMA, display scanlines, interrupts/timers, EEPROM and audio. Implement deterministic, bounded progression across frame boundaries; document any remaining instruction-granularity approximation. Do not double-charge memory transfers or starve the CPU.

### B. Hyper Voice and sound mixing

1. Implement the **Color/Crystal-only Hyper Voice** register behavior documented for 16-bit left/right output (`0x64–0x67`), 8-bit sample input (including `0x69`), and control/mode registers (`0x6A–0x6B`). Define documented masks, reset/readback semantics and relevant direct CPU writes. Do not invent unsupported behaviors for undocumented bits.
2. Implement the documented unsigned/signed sample extension variants, output shift/volume, sample-rate divisors, enable/reset, and stereo/mono left/right/both routing. Distinguish manual PCM writes from the SDMA-fed path where the hardware specifies different channel behavior.
3. Mix Hyper Voice with the legacy four channels on the **headphone stereo path** and keep the **internal speaker path** behavior distinct: Hyper Voice must not incorrectly appear through the built-in mono speaker. Maintain existing legacy voice/wavetable/noise/sweep behavior and respect output control (`0x91`), speaker volume (`0x9E`), channel output readbacks and documented bit widths/wrap behavior.
4. Improve current mixing/scaling only where necessary to accurately integrate these output paths (e.g., integer accumulator widths, signed PCM conversion, speaker/headphone selection and saturation/wrapping where specified). Keep the Rust-side `SAMPLE_RATE`/buffer contract stable unless a documented reason to change it is demonstrated; no extra JS synthesizer, arbitrary loudness boost, or unrelated audio redesign.
5. Keep browser output safe and bounded: existing Play/Load user-gesture activation, Mute/Unmute, volume slider, gain graph, pause/resume, tab visibility, and restart must work with newly emitted PCM without stale or duplicated buffers. An intentionally silent cartridge remains silent.

### C. Models, errors and documentation

- Scope **SDMA/Hyper Voice to Color and Crystal**; monochrome must retain hardware-appropriate I/O behavior, tested explicitly. Use the existing typed `Model` rather than ROM-specific detection.
- Accepted, documented register operations must perform real work; unsupported control combinations should fail with actionable diagnostics where behavior is truly unknown. Do not blanket-ignore or blanket-accept all of `0x4A–0x6B`.
- Update `docs/hardware-subset.md` with SDMA timing/rates/control/address semantics, Hyper Voice/mixing coverage, any approximations or remaining test-port gaps, and model-specific limitations. Update README/Settings help only if current compatibility claims need changing.

### D. Self-authored verification

- Add a **reproducible, CC0-licensed, source-included homebrew fixture** (or a small set of probes) that programs audio registers **using V30MZ machine instructions** and emits known PCM sequences. It must exercise SDMA → Channel 2, SDMA → Hyper Voice, and direct Hyper Voice writes; provide source/build instructions and clear expected register/audio outcomes.
- Do **not** ship commercial game ROMs, extracted music, downloaded wave samples, proprietary BIOS, or unlicensed binary files. Prefer deterministic PCM bytes generated by the existing fixture toolchain.
- Verify both the Rust core and the compiled WebAssembly/browser pipeline using actual generated sample buffers, not only assertions that output port writes were accepted.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] On Color and Crystal, correctly masked/readable SDMA `4A–4C, 4E–50, 52` I/O executes from V30MZ instructions with no unsupported-port fault. Source, length, shadow state, control modes and reserved-port behavior match documented semantics. Mono model behavior is tested and documented.
- [ ] Native tests cover all four sample rates; increment/decrement; RAM, ROM and SRAM sources including wait states; hold; zero-length rejection; one-shot completion; repeat; disable/re-enable; live/shadowed register edits; 20-bit wrap; and memory/bank boundaries.
- [ ] Timing tests verify the 128-clock SDMA cadence, the intended bus-steal cost and CPU stall, clock progression across frames, and interactions with General DMA, interrupts/timers, EEPROM and audio samples. There are no unbounded loops or double-charged CPU bus accesses.
- [ ] Hyper Voice tests cover both direct CPU PCM writes and SDMA input, signed/unsigned conversion, shift/rate modes, control reset, stereo and mono routing, and distinguish headphone from internal-speaker output; verify representative exact native sample values against independently calculated expected results.
- [ ] Regression tests verify existing four-channel wave/voice/sweep/noise, speaker/headphone mixing and output readbacks, legacy mono behavior, original playable demo completion on all three models, existing GDMA/save fixtures, and unchanged browser-local saves.
- [ ] One or more **original CC0 cartridge probes**, built reproducibly from included source, perform real sound-register programming through the emulated CPU and generate measurable **non-silent** output for Channel 2 and Hyper Voice. A browser test runs the same legal probe through Wasm and confirms its sample buffers/gain and proper pause/mute/restart behavior.
- [ ] Existing `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` pass (extend tests where appropriate). Report actual passes/failures/skips with reasons.
- [ ] `docs/hardware-subset.md`, fixture provenance and relevant user guidance precisely describe the supported modes and remaining inaccuracies. No commercial ROM/firmware, borrowed emulator core, game-specific conditions, unrelated framework, or frontend redesign is added.

Keep **one source Issue** for this sound-hardware milestone. Incremental commits/PRs are acceptable, but do not close it with dummy register handlers, silent Hyper Voice or untested timing.

## Optional validation

Compare sound and timing with a physical console or independently licensed homebrew audio tests; test other browsers/real speakers if available. These are helpful but are **not mandatory** because implementation and pre-merge acceptance can be tested using original fixtures. Audio quality by ear is not a substitute for native signal-level tests.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** After merge, record the existing `main` GitHub Pages workflow run and confirm the new build/deployment succeeds.
2. **Pending:** Open the unauthenticated public page, load the original CC0 sound probe locally and confirm normal sound activation, actual PCM output, mute/volume/pause/restart, and model selection without production-only errors. State accurately which observations were audible and which were measured by browser instrumentation.

Live-site deployment and production verification occur **after** merge and are not pre-merge gates.
